data.description: Familiarity with new data/metadata validation routines (metadata completeness, open-data readiness, API compliance) for dissemination artifacts.

data.justification: Officer must review not just data, but the metadata, actionable format, and accessibility of digital outputs, requiring knowledge of modern metadata/data validation.

data.description: Skill in reviewing, editing, and contextualizing auto-produced documentation, and creating user guidance on AI-enabled products/delivery platforms.

data.change to work: With major documentation and outputs auto-generated by AI, the Officer will shift to reviewing, adapting, and contextualizing AI-generated documentation for clarity or compliance, as well as preparing end-user training on new automated dissemination workflows.
data.justification: Officer must shift from creating documentation to reviewing/adapting AI-generated manuals and preparing training for next-gen dissemination tools.

data.description: Ability to articulate requirements for automated compilation and visualize/review the resulting products for both internal compliance and user fit-for-purpose.
data.historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'
data.change to work: Compiling and generating outputs is substantially automated; the focus becomes configuring requirements for system-driven compilation and reviewing outputs for appropriateness and user need.
data.justification: Systematically understanding how to specify requirements for and audit outputs created by AI—rather than doing the work directly.

data.description: Familiarity with open metadata, API-first platforms, discoverability protocols, and digital product design/selection as part of the output management process.
data.historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: 'Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada...', 'Knowledge of the divisional mandate... to adhere to various statistical and administrative practices... marketing and dissemination of statistical data.'
data.change to work: Expanding contextual knowledge to include awareness of metadata API, open data, and digital workflow standards relevant to dissemination and output selection.
data.justification: Officer needs not only source/data context, but strong knowledge of open metadata, discoverability, and standards for modern digital dissemination.

data.description: Skill in reviewing automation pipelines and the configuration/operation of modular dissemination components, including versioning, audit logging, and standards checks.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Shifts to ensuring QA, machine-actionability, and compliance of outputs published by automated dissemination modules; less manual formatting or ad hoc release, more focus on confirming process consistency and standards adherence.
data.justification: Tracking modular, automated digital components rather than managing outputs individually requires technical QA/oversight skills.

data.description: Knowledge of best practices and technical requirements for API-ready, modular, and automation-compliant output creation and management.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Shifts to ensuring QA, machine-actionability, and compliance of outputs published by automated dissemination modules; less manual formatting or ad hoc release, more focus on confirming process consistency and standards adherence.
data.justification: Outputs are now consumed by APIs, digital partners, and AI systems, not just humans; officer must understand their requirements.

data.description: Working knowledge of open data standards, APIs, metadata protocols, and automated/digital system QA.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
data.change to work: In addition to traditional quality review, must assess if dissemination components and their data products are compliant with open standards, machine-readable formats, robust metadata, and can be consumed/triggered using APIs and digital platforms.
data.justification: Need to technically review not just contents but interoperability, format, and metadata quality of digital outputs.

data.description: Able to communicate digital dissemination requirements to system developers, test new modules, and flag QA/process/standards issues as part of agile teams.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
data.change to work: Involvement shifts toward technical and process consultation—helping design, troubleshoot, and refine modular, automated dissemination infrastructure as part of team efforts, not manual product assembly.
data.justification: Must collaborate with IT, systems specialists, and automation engineers.

data.development area: Training in automation and digital dissemination
data.description: Knowledge and ability to explain the operation, limitations, and QA of automation-based dissemination, including use of API endpoints, automated version control, and exception handling.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
data.change to work: Contributes to and delivers training on automated dissemination systems, API-based delivery, use of modular tools, and standards compliance, rather than only manual process guides.
data.justification: Materials and training now focus on automation systems, not “manual how-to.”

data.description: Skill in systematically reviewing and validating AI/LLM-generated analytics, summaries, dashboards, ensuring clarity, rigor, and fitness for purpose.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Focuses on editing/validating draft outputs auto-generated by AI/LLM systems, with less hands-on original creation of content. Increases the need for critical review and QA of analytics and narrative reports.
data.justification: Officer must be able to review, correct, and approve machine-generated outputs, which requires understanding both their structure and potential errors/limitations.

data.description: Knowledge of how to review, edit, and translate AI/LLM-produced documentation for clarity, appropriateness, and full methodological transparency.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
data.change to work: Role changes from manual drafting to reviewing and contextualizing AI-generated reports/articles, ensuring methodological accuracy, narrative clarity, and client relevance.
data.justification: Officer must bridge between automated drafts (which may lack nuance/context) and the communication needs of diverse audiences.

data.development area: Critical interpretation and user-centered adaptation of AI output
data.description: Ability to assess machine-generated descriptive content for context, accuracy, messaging, and usability, making modifications for diverse stakeholders.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Summarizes and describes meaning of data.'
data.change to work: Instead of original summary, the officer assesses, tailors, and contextualizes AI-generated summaries for accuracy, audience comprehension, and statistical integrity.
data.justification: Critical thinking is needed to augment, clarify, and correct draft outputs—recognizing where the machine narrative may be insufficient or misleading.

data.description: Ability to read, interpret, and contextualize reports/flags produced by AI/ML-driven QA tools, and determine required follow-up action.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
data.change to work: Shifts from hands-on validation/checking to reviewing, adjudicating, and contextualizing automated QA results; involved in refining validation standards, thresholds, and escalation criteria.
data.justification: Officer needs skills in interpreting automated QA diagnostics, anomaly/outlier reports, and in setting thresholds for further action/escalation.

data.development area: Validation protocol analysis and system feedback
data.description: Skill in critically analyzing automated validation rules and procedures, suggesting improvements, and helping tune AI/ML tools for domain needs.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
data.change to work: Shifts from hands-on validation/checking to reviewing, adjudicating, and contextualizing automated QA results; involved in refining validation standards, thresholds, and escalation criteria.
data.justification: Must play a role in system feedback—improving AI/ML QA processes based on recurring errors, edge cases, or shifting data/context.

data.description: Understanding of AI/ML approaches to data quality validation, anomaly detection, and benchmarking, with ability to evaluate accuracy and contextual appropriateness.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness.'
data.change to work: Now involves oversight of automated validation, focusing on exception handling and improvement of automated benchmarking/consistency logic.
data.justification: Officer must know how to guide machine-driven evaluation and provide feedback loops into system learning.

data.description: Ability to review and resolve uncertainty in privacy/SCD actions taken by AI, including nuanced judgment in ambiguous or novel output types.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Editing and validation tasks are now centered on reviewing disclosure and privacy compliance in automated outputs; typical manual intervention is for flagged exceptions.
data.justification: Officer must interpret and adjudicate complex AI-flagged disclosure risks, often in new, ambiguous, or critical cases.

data.development area: Automated SCD systems and audit trails
data.description: Understanding of how privacy/SCD tools function, what is logged, and how to document, supplement, or override their actions and rationales in complex compliance scenarios.
data.historic work: Technical Activities/Skills: 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts... and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.'
data.change to work: Role pivots to ensuring automation aligns with all applicable privacy/SCD legal/policy frameworks, and to documenting, auditing, and justifying human interventions for privacy compliance.
data.justification: The Officer must audit, validate, and, if needed, modify the rationale and documentation auto-generated by SCD tools, ensuring compliance.

data.development area: Output package quality assurance and sign-off
data.description: Ability to systematically review all components of an automated output package (narrative, metadata, technical notes, translations), and to confidently approve release or manage/resolve anomalies and exceptions.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: The focus is now on vetting and approving automation-assembled output packages (rather than preparing/disseminating them manually), intervening in special cases, and ensuring appropriate communication/documentation accompanies the release.
data.justification: Critical review and sign-off of complete, automation-assembled output packages (including supporting documentation and metadata) requires advanced QA oversight skills.

data.development area: Automated output integration and completeness review
data.description: Knowledge of what constitutes a complete, high-quality, and compliant automated statistical output package—including multi-lingual requirements, uncertainty metrics, and all supporting appendices.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables, and other output.'
data.change to work: Instead of compiling outputs, Officer verifies the completeness, integration, and appropriateness of automation-prepared outputs, and reviews the supporting contextual narrative and technical appendices.
data.justification: Increased need to understand and validate complex, multi-source output packages to ensure each element is properly incorporated and documented by automation.

data.development area: Digital dissemination systems oversight and troubleshooting
data.description: Ability to audit, validate, and escalate issues in automated dissemination pipelines—including exceptions, platform errors, or complex user access scenarios.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Duties move toward oversight and QA of automated dissemination; the Officer becomes responsible for approvals, troubleshooting, and digital platform QA, rather than hands-on dissemination tasks.
data.justification: Officer must monitor, diagnose, and improve automated systems, and interface across business/IT boundaries on exception scenarios.

data.development area: API/digital platform and metadata enrichment protocols
data.description: Understanding how API-delivered outputs, advanced metadata tagging, and AI-agent searchability work in modern dissemination platforms; ability to advise on standards, upgrades, and user impact.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
data.change to work: Focus of participation shifts to collaborating on digital-first workflow updates, advising on metadata enrichment and API-channel design, and supporting platform evolution and standards adoption.
data.justification: Deeper technical and policy knowledge required to collaborate on digital and API-first platform design, rollout, and QA.

data.development area: Digital dissemination user support and training expertise
data.description: Expertise in training/support related to API-first dissemination and real-time digital product access, for both staff and data users adapting to new digital release modalities.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
data.change to work: Training/support must now emphasize API and digital-first dissemination, AI discoverability, and automation-driven change management for users (internal and external).
data.justification: New/advanced training content is required for digital system users, focusing on automation, APIs, machine-actionable metadata, and modern dissemination workflows.

data.development area: Automated metadata and linkage standards and QA
data.description: Up-to-date knowledge of metadata standards, discoverability schemas, and the functioning of automated data/content loading and output linking systems.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata.'
data.change to work: Role pivots to meta-validation: checking completeness, enrichment, API/AI actionability, and automated linkage of metadata; less hands-on, more oversight/troubleshooting/reporting.
data.justification: Need to understand, audit, and validate compliance with digital/automated metadata, linkage, and discoverability standards.

data.description: Skill in supporting, diagnosing, and optimizing access to outputs for both human and automated users in a digital, API-first landscape.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
data.change to work: Emphasis shifts to consulting on, and troubleshooting, machine-actionable outputs, API access, and discoverability—supporting power users, developers, and advanced human/AI clients; must be able to diagnose failures in digital product access.
data.justification: Requirements for advanced advisory and diagnostic skills related to API, AI, and machine-actionable data use.

data.description: Skill in systematically reviewing, validating, and customizing AI/LLM-generated dissemination products for publication, metadata, and audience standards.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Primary tasks now involve reviewing for adherence to publication, meta, and audience-specific standards; less generation by hand, more focus on standards QA, final adaptation, and sign-off.
data.justification: Must be able to interpret, critique, and adapt a wide range of AI/automation-derived outputs (text, graphics, microdata, etc.) for diverse audiences.

data.development area: Automated workflow and product pipeline logic
data.description: Understanding how automation assembles, enriches, and finalizes dissemination products; ability to give effective feedback and suggest workflow improvements for special requirements.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'
data.change to work: Transition from compiling to reviewing/reshaping multi-source, automation-created outputs (including troubleshooting or specifying refinements in AI workflows for special cases, e.g., for PUMF or complex graphics).
data.justification: Officer must understand the system’s logic for assembling outputs and participate in feedback/improvement for the automation pipeline.

data.development area: Exception management and high-visibility release liaison
data.description: Ability to review and approve exception cases in digital orchestration systems, and to coordinate confidential/embargoed or impactful public releases with stakeholders.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
data.change to work: Role focuses on policy review, exception workflows, and special-case product releases (e.g., embargo, retraction, or high-visibility clients), much less on routine operational work.
data.justification: Officer needs skills in navigating, auditing, and managing digital release workflows and exception approval, as well as in communicating with high-level clients.

data.development area: Secure access management and client liaison
data.description: Skill in granting, auditing, and managing secure digital access to confidential or embargoed data, and in advanced client communication for sensitive releases.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
data.change to work: Duties now center on high-level user support and consultation (e.g., secure research access, press briefings for embargoed releases, subscriber communications), as standard release channels are largely hands-free.
data.justification: Greater responsibility for managing access for diverse, privileged user groups in API-enabled, secure digital environments.

data.description: Skill in reviewing, validating, and adapting content, strategy, and channel selection generated by AI for promotional outreach, including campaign performance monitoring.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Markets and disseminates data.'
data.change to work: Role shifts to reviewing and optimizing AI-generated outreach campaigns across platforms, and taking ownership for sensitive or high-impact communications.
data.justification: Must critically evaluate and intervene on AI-prompted messages for clarity, alignment, and risk.

data.description: Knowledge of effective AI-driven outreach strategies, and how to review, adapt, or supplement messaging for interpretation accuracy, compliance, or complex audience needs.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
data.change to work: Work shifts to editing/validating AI-generated language for promos and assuring correct interpretation/messaging in outreach products.
data.justification: Reviewing, customizing, or rejecting AI-generated marketing and communication text requires greater skill in risk assessment, narrative tone, and public/audience centricity.

data.description: Ability to handle, resolve, and document nuanced, ambiguous, or policy-sensitive user issues, working in tandem with automated systems and tracking knowledgebase/FAQ impacts.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
data.change to work: Most queries are routine and answered by automation. Officer’s consultative role is reserved for escalated, non-routine, nuanced, or strategic requests, as well as designing/curating advanced support pathways.
data.justification: Officer requires skill at diagnosing and resolving complex digital support issues, including those only surfaced after automation fails.

data.description: Proficiency in reviewing and editing AI-generated FAQ content, training staff and power users on automated support, and feeding user insights back into digital service design.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
data.change to work: Provides ongoing review of AI-generated knowledge articles, populates advanced FAQ material, and supports training/advice for both users and staff in the new automated support ecosystem.
data.justification: Greater need for digital literacy in chatbot/AI knowledge curation, and in content review/editing for automated support channels.

data.description: Ability to interpret, validate, and provide expert input on AI- or automation-generated needs analyses, material, and business case recommendations.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
data.change to work: This element will now require the EC-02 to review, interpret, and validate automated analytical and needs-synthesis material generated by AI. The task shifts from raw preparation to higher-level critical review of pre-assembled material.
data.justification: Current expectations assume manual synthesis/preparation; future role requires ability to critically review AI-generated inputs, recognize limitations/gaps, and contextualize automated findings.

data.description: Knowledge of how AI generates, detects, or highlights statistical trends, including its potential blind spots, bias, or error types, to inform when expert override or supplementation is required.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
data.change to work: Rather than relying solely on manual review/statistical output, trend and development identification will be supported by AI-driven scanning and synthesis tools. EC-02's role becomes assessing, interpreting, and prioritizing AI-generated trend findings.
data.justification: Recognizing when and how AI-mapped trends require additional expert insight or contextualization, and understanding how to tune or direct AI tools for improved output.

data.description: Skill in integrating AI-suggested feedback and recommendations with human subject matter expertise, including validation, contextualization, and clear communication for survey improvement.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
data.change to work: Suggesting feedback for improvements is now rooted in interpreting AI-synthesized analyses of collection and processing methods. EC-02 will validate, contextualize, and translate these insights for practical application.
data.justification: Ability to integrate automated recommendations with subject matter expertise for actionable feedback—knowing when AI output needs moderation, augmentation, or clarification for process improvement.

data.description: Ability to evaluate, critique, and where needed adjust AI-generated feasibility studies and impact assessments, bridging automated outputs with nuanced program realities.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
data.change to work: Assessment and feasibility evaluation for new or modified programs will involve deep interaction with automated tools for initial synthesis and modeling of needs/scenarios. The work will emphasize the interpretation and adjustment of AI-drafted materials.
data.justification: Knowing how to assess the scope and technical foundation of AI-drafted feasibility studies and recommendations—spotting errors, oversights, or need for expert contextual correction.

data.development area: Synthesis of AI-driven and Expert Process Evaluation
data.description: Skill in balancing automated analysis results with expert knowledge to develop, communicate, and justify improvements to processes and systems.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
data.change to work: Research/analysis activities are increasingly launched from AI/automation-flagged issues and results. The EC-02 will increasingly propose changes based on the synthesis of AI diagnosis, reserving manual evaluation for higher-order complexities.
data.justification: Ability to use, adapt, and supplement AI-detected process weaknesses or gaps, ensuring recommendations remain relevant and are not over-influenced by algorithmic limitations.

data.development area: Awareness of AI Data Sourcing and Reliability
data.description: Understanding the structure, coverage, and potential gaps in data sources as used by AI/automation for needs analysis, including methods to supplement or correct automated data synthesis.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.
data.change to work: EC-02 must now also understand how AI systems interface with and pull from multiple data sources, including their constraints and curation for automated needs synthesis.
data.justification: Familiarity with the limits of AI-access to data assets, and what steps are needed to ensure reliability and comprehensiveness in automated synthesizing.

data.description: Ability to review, critique, and contextualize needs/trends identified by AI tools, and to intervene where additional data, nuance, or subject-matter assessment is required.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Identifies statistical trends and developments.
data.change to work: This task now starts with AI-generated outputs (trend lists, priority signals, benchmarks from external sources). The EC-02 evaluates, contextualizes, and refines these outputs for program decision-making.
data.justification: The skill gap is the move from direct/manual trend identification to expert validation/interpretation of AI-flagged needs and developments, including knowing when to trust, challenge, or augment automation outputs.

data.description: Skill in interrogating, validating, and integrating AI-generated findings when forming constructive feedback, proposals, and recommendations.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
data.change to work: Feedback and recommendations are increasingly based on synthesis of automated needs analysis and benchmarking, requiring the EC-02 to specialize in interpreting, qualifying, and supplementing automated needs assessments for survey/method change proposals.
data.justification: Gap arises because feedback is no longer based primarily on manual investigation/review but on automated, sometimes opaque AI analytics.

data.description: Understanding of how AI/automation operationalizes statistical theories and international benchmarks for need identification, to ensure oversight and improvement of tools used.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
data.change to work: The EC-02 must now also understand the interaction of AI-driven inputs and international best practices (e.g., automatically benchmarked recommendations), with a need to assess how statistical theory is operationalized and interpreted via automation.
data.justification: Need to supplement domain knowledge with literacy in how statistical/economic principles are instantiated in AI scanning and benchmarking tools.

data.description: Ability to dynamically integrate automated research/analysis outputs with expert-driven inquiry, especially when AI signals limitations in emerging/complex needs.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
data.change to work: With automation doing initial scanning and proposal, EC-02's research and analysis must focus on higher-order review of AI-flagged issues, and on exploring emerging or complex scenarios that may not be covered by algorithms.
data.justification: Requires an ability to operate flexibly between automated insight and higher-level analytic thinking, with comfort in AI oversight and intervention.

data.description: Ability to assess quality, interpret, and escalate user needs and feedback synthesized by automated systems, with direct user engagement as needed for complex or high-priority issues.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
data.change to work: Provision of data/assistance is now mediated by an AI-driven consultation interface (e.g., user feedback synthesis, chatbots, summary dashboards). EC-02 is responsible for overseeing the quality of support, interpreting priority cases, and stepping in for user support in ambiguous or complex scenarios.
data.justification: Move from manual user support/data provision to oversight of AI-moderated communication, plus intervention in exception/priority cases.

data.description: Skill in validating and contextualizing AI-aggregated requirements, prioritizing them, and negotiating procedural adjustments or clarifications in partnership with automation outputs.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: Communication: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
data.change to work: Liaison now includes interpreting requirements identified via AI automation, validating accuracy and completeness, and negotiating contextual details with users and subject matter experts only for cases requiring expert input. Routine translation/negotiation of requirements is automated except for nuanced or complex cases.
data.justification: Skill needs shift from basic liaison and translation of requirements to critical validation of AI-generated specifications and skilled negotiation over ambiguities or priorities.

data.description: Knowledge of where human intervention is needed to supplement, confirm, or correct AI-synthesized needs and requirements based on deep contextual program understanding.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.
data.change to work: Contextual expertise is still vital, but its use refocuses on validating, clarifying, and supplementing needs assessments automatically surfaced by AI tools—ensuring human insight fills automation gaps and helps set priorities.
data.justification: Requires blending domain/contextual expertise with understanding of automated consultation systems and how/where they may misinterpret or overlook important contextual details.

data.development area: AI Output Quality and Compliance Validation
data.description: Ability to critically assess and refine AI-generated output objectives and accompanying quality measures for compliance with legal frameworks, organizational strategy, and user needs.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
data.change to work: Analysis and preparation of analytical material now starts from AI/automation-generated objectives (drafts, proposed measures), which the EC-02 validates for compliance, completeness, and contextual appropriateness.
data.justification: Gap is between current manual drafting versus critical appraisal/validation role for AI-generated objectives and documentation.

data.development area: Strategic and Legal Adjudication in Automated Workflows
data.description: Ability to judge, escalate, and resolve strategic, legal, or ethical trade-offs surfaced by AI-driven proposal generation; ensure compliance and appropriateness in all analytical outputs.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
data.change to work: Feedback and recommendations for objectives focus on strategic and compliance issues detected in AI-generated material, moving staff up the value chain toward final approval and risk management.
data.justification: Now requires expert judgment regarding the sufficiency of automated drafts and an ability to escalate/adjust issues that are not resolved in automation.

data.development area: AI Process and Output Objective Literacy
data.description: Deepened understanding of how AI applications create, reference, and propose objectives, including where system limitations may affect legal/methodological compliance.
data.historic work: Technical Activities / Skills / Responsibilities / Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
data.change to work: Validation of outputs now includes strong emphasis on understanding how AI applications and automations assemble and draft output and quality objectives; must critically interrogate the technical underpinnings of automated objective-setting.
data.justification: Additional technical/system knowledge required to spot where AI-generated objectives may miss domain specifics or legal nuances.

data.development area: Final Concept Specification and AI Validation
data.description: Ability to critically evaluate AI-generated conceptual inputs, make theoretically/statistically informed selections, justify final specifications, and formally certify concepts for process use.
data.historic work: Key Activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
data.change to work: Preparation starts from AI pre-synthesized options for concepts. The EC-02 is responsible for detailed review, selection, refinement, and official sign-off, with increased focus on theoretical and statistical adequacy.

Officers are responsible for configuring or adapting workflow settings as needed for unique cases, and for overseeing automated orchestration and escalation protocols.
data.justification: Hands-on skills for digital workflow management and configuration are essential, including using business process management platforms and automated orchestration tools.

data.development area: Assessment and Documentation of Digital Workflow Requirements
data.description: Skill in evaluating, specifying, and documenting digital workflow, orchestration, automation compatibility, and monitoring needs for various business processes.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.'
data.change to work: System requirement assessments now focus on digital workflow orchestration, compatibility with modular automation, and oversight of AI monitoring functions. Officers may be tasked with documenting requirements and evaluating the effectiveness of system designs in sustaining real-time, automated operations.
data.justification: Evaluation and documentation of system requirements shift toward digital, modular workflow platforms and their alignment to automation standards.

data.development area: Modular Digital Workflow Analysis and Automation Design
data.description: Expertise in digital workflow analysis and automation system design, including orchestration logic, modular integration, and exception management.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages...'
data.change to work: Systems analysis and design now require specialized knowledge of modular, digital workflow orchestration, including APIs, event-driven triggers, AI monitoring, and exception escalation routines.
data.justification: Systems analysis and design capabilities must address automated workflow integration, real-time orchestration, and modular system architectures.

data.description: Capacity to analyze, interpret, and report automated test outputs, audit logs, incident escalations, and to recommend automation or process improvements.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.'
data.change to work: Analysis and reporting now focus on outcomes of automated, continuous system tests, critical review of audit trails and test logs, and the escalation of findings and recommendations that address automation gaps or policy compliance issues.
data.justification: Requires skills in interpreting digital, automated test outputs and identifying compliance/risk gaps, along with digital incident management reporting.

data.development area: Automated Test Pipeline Supervision and Go-Live Oversight
data.description: Skill in high-level readiness review, risk analysis, and sign-off for automated system qualification and live deployment.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Testing participation now means high-level supervision, review and sign-off of automated system readiness outputs, and direct intervention only in escalated automation failures or regulatory concerns.
data.justification: Ability to supervise automated test pipeline readiness and provide critical sign-off and intervention when required.

data.development area: Automated Test Integration and Compliance Evaluation
data.description: Advanced knowledge in evaluating the adequacy, completeness, and compliance of automated testing pipelines for system review and improvement.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.'
data.change to work: Assessment and review now address the adequacy of automated testing logic and tools, and evaluate how they align with overall system requirements and regulatory frameworks.
data.justification: Systems assessment now must cover automated test integration, QA procedures, and compliance assurance.

data.development area: AI-Driven Pilot Supervision and Feedback Analysis
data.description: Expertise in reviewing, interpreting, and reporting automated pilot results, escalating issues, and supporting iterative process redesign decisions.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.'
data.change to work: Analysis and reporting shift to interpreting AI-automated pilot feedback, identifying and escalating non-routine process or data issues, synthesizing iterative findings, and validating process redesign proposals.
data.justification: Requires advanced skill in interpreting digital, AI-driven monitoring feedback and translating synthesized process analytics into actionable reports and recommendations.

data.development area: Digital Pilot Supervision and Go/No-Go Decision-Making
data.description: Skill in supervising digital pilot runs, managing exception escalation, evaluating results, and providing final approval for process advancement.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Role centers on high-level supervision, sign-off, and exception management during digitally orchestrated pilot cycles; direct manual piloting is replaced by monitoring automated pilot execution and analysis.
data.justification: Need for skills in oversight, sign-off, and exception management in automated pilot environments.

data.development area: Iterative Analysis Integration and Impact Assessment
data.description: Ability to correlate automated pilot analytics and feedback to overall process integrity, completeness, and adaptation requirements.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.'
data.change to work: Must be able to relate pilot feedback from automated data and instrument validation to downstream operational impacts, integrity, and completeness, integrating rapid cycle analytical insights.
data.justification: Ability to synthesize iterative pilot/feedback data with downstream integrity and process impact requirements.

data.description: Skill in reviewing, supplementing, and validating auto-generated technical documentation, manuals, training packages, and onboarding resources for accuracy and user relevance.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.'
data.change to work: Manual writing is replaced with review, supplementation, and validation of AI-generated documentation and training materials. Officers ensure technical accuracy, relevance, and accessibility for users.
data.justification: Skills shift from manual writing to critical review and curation of digitally-generated documentation and training resources.

data.development area: Collaboration with Digital Training and Onboarding Systems
data.description: Skills for integrating operational expertise into automated training modules, evaluating AI-driven onboarding, and supporting user adaptation to digital learning environments.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.'
data.change to work: Training input is now focused on integrating domain expertise into digital learning modules and AI-driven onboarding processes, and facilitating user adaptation to automated training delivery.
data.justification: Requires knowledge and practical skills for collaborating with digital training designers, reviewing automated modules, and supporting user transition to digital onboarding.

data.development area: Automated Production Readiness and Onboarding Evaluation
data.description: Ability to assess deployment compliance, validate production readiness, and evaluate the effectiveness and completeness of digital documentation and training materials.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.'
data.change to work: Reports and recommendations now focus on deployment compliance, system validation, issues surfaced during automated move to production, and performance of digital documentation and onboarding systems.
data.justification: Ability to evaluate automated deployment outcomes, identify issues for escalation, and recommend adjustments to automated documentation/training resources.

data.development area: Oversight and Compliance in Automated Production Environments
data.description: Skill in monitoring automated deployment, validating regulatory and operational compliance, and managing exception escalation during system launch and onboarding.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Role focuses on oversight and compliance validation for the automated deployment and live monitoring of systems, with manual activity limited to exception handling and policy-related review.
data.justification: Expanded oversight and compliance validation skillset required for automated production environments.

data.development area: Passive and Automated Data Collection Oversight
data.description: Skill in validating operation, troubleshooting exceptions, maintaining compliance, and ensuring data quality in digital, AI-enabled passive collection systems.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Role is now focused on monitoring, validating, and maintaining passive/automated intake processes, including oversight of APIs, automated feeds, digital integrations, and real-time data validation. Manual involvement is limited to exceptions and special cases.
data.justification: Need for proficiency in supervising, troubleshooting, and validating automated/passive intake processes, including oversight of digital interfaces and data feeds.

data.development area: User Support for Digital Collection Systems
data.description: Ability to support, train, and advise users on passive/automated data collection systems, including set-up, integration issues, and technical troubleshooting.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.'
data.change to work: Assistance and advice is now centered on digital collection technologies, passive data interfaces, interpretation of automated intake processes, and troubleshooting technical collection issues.
data.justification: Need to advise users on technical setup, integration, and troubleshooting of digital, automated collection platforms and passive data sources.

data.development area: Digital Liaison and Passive Data Integration Facilitation
data.description: Skill in facilitating passive data integration and troubleshooting with external data suppliers for digital intake systems.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.'
data.change to work: Contact now focuses on supplier readiness for passive data integration, troubleshooting API or data feed problems, and clarifying digital-provision requirements rather than conventional survey reminders.
data.justification: Communication must now deal with digital integration, passive provisioning, and technical problem-solving for external data sources.

data.development area: Automated Data Quality Assurance and Exception Handling
data.description: Ability to verify data quality and compliance in digital, automated, and passive intake environments, managing exception escalation and resolution.
data.historic work: Skills: 'Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.'
data.change to work: Data verification now focuses on overseeing automated real-time validation routines and digital QA of passive intake pipelines.
data.justification: Must have knowledge and skill for digital, automated data quality assurance and exception validation.

data.development area: Digital Systems Integration and Passive Data Flow Analysis
data.description: Comprehensive understanding of digital system integration for passive intake, real-time data flow analysis, and event-driven automation configuration.
data.historic work: Skills: 'Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows...'
data.change to work: Systems analysis expands to include passive data interfaces (APIs, feeds, digital exhaust), real-time digital data flows, and validation logic for automated collection.
data.justification: New knowledge required for digital system integration, passive data flow analysis, and real-time event management.

data.development area: Automation-Enabled System Setup and Flexible Workforce Management
data.description: Skills in supervising AI-enabled system configuration, metadata compliance checks, and dynamic workforce allocation platforms.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Participates in the oversight and validation of automated setup and ingestion systems, metadata compliance, and AI-assisted workforce allocation (rather than classic static role deployment). Manual setup is rare and reserved for exceptions.
data.justification: Must develop skills for validating, troubleshooting, and maintaining digitally automated setup routines, ingestion platforms, and dynamic workforce allocation tools.

data.development area: Digital Setup Reporting and Metadata Compliance Analysis
data.description: Skill in preparing digital system setup reports, analyzing metadata compliance, and recommending enhancements to automation and workforce management routines.
data.historic work: Technical Activities: 'Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.'
data.change to work: Reports and recommendations shift to issues around automation effectiveness in setup and acquisition, metadata compliance gaps, workforce cross-training and system adaptation for digital-first implementation.
data.justification: Expanded digital competency for evaluating, recommending, and reporting automated setup and metadata compliance issues.

data.development area: Digital Training Support and Workforce Upskilling
data.description: Ability to contribute to digital automation training material, deliver support for dynamic resource adaptation, and facilitate cross-training programs.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.'
data.change to work: Input now needed for digital training modules focused on automation setup, AI-enabled tools, metadata validation, and dynamic resource allocation. Delivery may include virtual/interactive environments.
data.justification: Practical knowledge required in supporting digital-first training and onboarding, including upskilling staff for dynamic allocation and automation routines.

data.description: Skill in using digital and AI-enabled tools to check, validate, and maintain minimum metadata compliance during collection setup.
data.historic work: Skills: 'Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.'
data.change to work: Tasks now include verifying that system setup supports metadata compliance and data reliability using automated routines.
data.justification: Knowledge and skill in digital metadata verification and automated compliance checking required.

data.development area: Integration of Automation and Adaptive Workforce Systems
data.description: Understanding of integrated digital setup routines, metadata-first design, AI-based extraction/validation, and cross-training/dynamic allocation platforms.
data.historic work: Skills: 'Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows...'
data.change to work: System analysis now includes automation/AI-enabled setup, metadata data flows, and platforms for dynamic resource/reallocation. Expertise required in these digital operational layers.
data.justification: Expanded knowledge of digital operational system setup, including automation/AI integration and digital workforce management tools.

data.development area: Digital Collection Oversight and Exception Management
data.description: Ability to monitor AI/automation dashboards, resolve collection exceptions, and maintain high data quality in a digital, automated environment.
data.historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.'
data.change to work: Direct manual collection is replaced by oversight and monitoring of digital collection workflows, active management of exception cases, and continuous review of AI-optimized resource strategies.
data.justification: Skills required for real-time supervision and troubleshooting of AI-driven collection and case management platforms.

data.development area: Technical Support for Digital Collection Integration

This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.'
data.change to work: External contact now centers on supporting integration and troubleshooting of digital pipelines for passive administrative sources, or resolving exceptions in automated survey operations.
data.justification: Need proficiency in technical troubleshooting, digital integration support, and communicating new digital-first collection requirements.

data.development area: Analytics and Reporting of Digital Collection Performance

data.justification: Ability to interpret and present digital collection performance metrics.

data.development area: Digital Data Quality Assurance and Metadata Validation

data.change to work: Data verification focuses on real-time, automated validation mechanisms and continuous monitoring of AI-generated metadata and tagging.
data.justification: Must be knowledgeable in digital QA protocols, AI-driven validation, and automated metadata management.

data.development area: Digital Pipeline Architecture and AI Resource Optimization
data.description: Comprehensive understanding of digital collection infrastructure, workflow automation, and real-time resource management principles.
data.historic work: Skills: 'Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows...'
data.change to work: Analysis and design skills broaden to cover digital collection pipeline architecture, integration of AI-driven case management, and resource allocation logic.
data.justification: Knowledge of digital infrastructure, AI-platform integration, and real-time resource optimization algorithms.
